findings.message: The diff changes plugin code under plugins/specclaw-fleet (new commands, a new image layout, new pipelines, new skills). It bumps none of the shared versions: plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json, and every plugins[] entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. Bump all of them together to one new version.
findings.scenario: The PR is merged with plugin.json and marketplace.json unchanged. Installed copies of specclaw-fleet stay at the old version and never pick up doctor, trigger or the new skills, and the repo's all-plugins-one-version invariant has no new version to hold to.

findings.message: The gates run against the operator's local working tree, but the default path only queues the pipeline. `az pipelines run` is given no change name, so the pipeline scans and dispatches every approved change on `FLEET_REF`, and does nothing for this one if its state.json on that branch is not approved or not at phase 'proposal'. Trigger still prints `{ok:true, mode:pipeline, run:...}`, so 'queued' reads as 'will be dispatched'. Pass the change to the pipeline as a parameter, or verify that the pushed ref carries the approval before reporting success.
findings.scenario: The operator approves change A locally and does not push, then runs `trigger A`. The gates pass and the run id is printed. The pipeline checks out main, sees A as not approved, and dispatches nothing. Separately, an approved change B that nobody triggered, on main, gets dispatched or tagged fleet:refused by the same run.

findings.message: `trigger_gates` repeats the dispatch gate sequence (assignee, fleet:auto consent, credential lookup) and takes the agent from the operator's local `FLEET_DEFAULT_AGENT`. The pipeline dispatches with its own `fleetDefaultAgent` variable. The two copies can pick different agents. Trigger also skips the codex-busy check. Pass an explicit agent to the pipeline, or reuse `check_gates`.
findings.scenario: The pipeline sets fleetDefaultAgent=codex. The operator's environment has no FLEET_DEFAULT_AGENT, so trigger checks the claude credential, which the assignee has. The gate passes and the run is queued. The pipeline's dispatch then refuses for a missing codex credential and tags the item fleet:refused.

findings.message: The hosted agent clones specclaw from github.com/chan4lk/specclaw at `fleetSpecclawRef`, a mutable tag name. That code then runs with the kube service connection and the ARM service principal. The commit actually executed is never recorded. Resolve the ref to a full commit SHA, pin to the SHA, and log it.
findings.scenario: The tag fleet-v0.8.9 is force-moved, or the tag is recreated on a different commit. The next hosted run executes different dispatch code with the cluster and vault credentials. Nothing records which commit ran.

findings.message: Only rc==1 counts as a failure. Rc 2 means skip, and any other non-zero rc (a crashed check or a missing command) is silently treated as passing. A skipped item also still ends in 'doctor: all checks ok'. Count every non-zero rc other than 2 as a failure, and print the skip count in the summary.
findings.scenario: A check function exits 127 or 3 because of a bug. Doctor counts it as passing and exits 0. A non-GHCR image is never verified, yet the output says 'all checks ok'.

findings.message: Every `fetch_claude` failure is recorded as exit=claude-verify-failed: a network or egress failure, a missing platform, and a signature mismatch. The run skill tells people this is an infrastructure or gate stop. Egress to downloads.claude.ai at pod runtime is also not visibly allowlisted: the diff touches no Squid or k8s config. Report fetch failures separately from verification failures.
findings.scenario: The proxy does not allow downloads.claude.ai. Every claude job fails with 'claude-verify-failed', which points at tampering instead of a blocked host.

findings.message: The 'no side effects' check looks for `azdo-issue (fields|tag|claim)`. That pattern does not match `untag` or `create`, so a refusal that creates or untags would still pass. Add untag and create to the pattern.
findings.scenario: A gate is reordered so `--retry` untags before the consent check. Every gate test still passes.

findings.message: The README says refusals have no side effects, but `trigger --create` creates the work item before the assignee and consent gates run. A newly created work item has no assignee, so the first `--create` run always creates the item and then refuses. Fix the wording or move creation after the gates.
findings.scenario: `trigger X --create` on a change with no work item creates the item, then exits 1 with 'has no assignee'. The item now exists, contradicting the README.

findings.message: `. "$SPECCLAW_DIR/.env"` executes the file as shell with `set -a`. Parse KEY=VALUE lines instead of sourcing.
findings.scenario: A .env that contains `$(cmd)` or a stray line runs that code with the operator's az and kube credentials when they run trigger.
